memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac, who then lived near Beer Lahai Roi." - Gen 25:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham is gone, but God is not. The moment his great father dies, we read, "After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac." The blessing did not die with Abraham. God simply carried His faithfulness forward to the next generation.

This is deeply reassuring. We sometimes lean so heavily on a godly parent, mentor, or leader that we wonder how we will manage without them. But our hope was never really in that person — it was in the God who stood behind them. When they are gone, God remains, and His blessing continues.

Notice too where Isaac chose to live: near Beer Lahai Roi, "the well of the Living One who sees me." Isaac settled by a place that testified God sees His people. He was making his life near the reminder that God was watching over him personally, not only over his father.

You may be walking a road without someone who once carried you. Take heart. The same God who blessed those before you is fully able to bless you now. His faithfulness is not inherited property that runs out; it is fresh mercy for every generation (Lam 3:22-23). Settle your life near the truth that the living God sees you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trusting God Himself, or leaning too heavily on a person?
2. Do I live near the reminder that "the Living One sees me"?
3. How has God shown fresh faithfulness in my own generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your blessing does not run out with those who go before me. Help me to trust You directly, knowing You see me and go with me. Amen.
